result.topic_en: Calculations on shock (discontinuity) speeds in one-dimensional gas flow, with jump conditions involving density ratios, a special case with $\varrho_2=1$, $\varrho_1=\alpha^2$, and the characteristic variables p, q expressed in terms of $\alpha$.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x_1' + a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1}} = x_2' + a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2}}$ $\varrho_1 > \varrho_2$ $x_1' > x_2'$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x_1' - a$

$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x_1' [-+-] - a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1}} = x_2' - a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2}}$ $\varrho_1 < \varrho_2$ $x_1' > x_2'$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x_2' + a$
[figure: two curves crossing coordinate axes]

[-$x < 0$ $x_1'$ $\varrho = \alpha^2$ $x > 0$ $x_2' = 0$ $\varrho = 1$-]

[-$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t}$-] $\varrho_2 = 1$ $x_2' = 0$ $\alpha > 1$
$\varrho_1 = \alpha^2$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x_1' + \frac{a}{\alpha} = a\alpha$ $\frac{x_1'}{a} = \alpha - \frac{1}{\alpha}$ [?]
$dq : dp = (\alpha-1)^2 : (1+\alpha)^2$
$4p = \alpha - \frac{1}{\alpha} + 2\log\alpha = \int_1^\alpha (1+\frac{1}{\alpha})^2 \partial\alpha$ =
$4q = \alpha - \frac{1}{\alpha} - 2\log\alpha = \int_1^\alpha (1-\frac{1}{\alpha})^2 \partial\alpha$
[faint: $\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x' + a$ [?]] , $q = $ const.
$\frac{x'}{a} = -\log\varrho + \alpha - \frac{1}{\alpha} + 2\log\alpha$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x' - a$ $x = (x' - a)t$ $x = a(\alpha - \frac{1}{\alpha} - 1)t$, $x = a\alpha t$.

$\alpha > 1$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} = x' + \frac{a}{\alpha} = a\alpha$
$2(p+q) + e^{q-p} - e^{p-q} = 0$
$dp(2 - \frac{1}{\alpha} - \alpha) + dq(2 + \frac{1}{\alpha} + \alpha)$
$dp(\alpha-1)^2 = dq(\alpha+1)^2$ $= 0$

$\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} - (x'+a)\right)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}\partial q + \left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} - (x'-a)\right)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}dp = 0$
$(\frac{1}{\alpha} - 1)\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}\partial q + (\frac{1}{\alpha}+1)\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}dp = 0$
$\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}(1-\alpha)^3 + \frac{\partial t}{\partial p}(1+\alpha)^3 = 0$

methods.what: Special case: gas at rest with unit density ahead, density $\alpha^2$ behind; shock speed $a\alpha$
Riemann invariants p, q across the shock expressed as functions of $\alpha$ via integrals
Velocity expressed via log density (isothermal Riemann invariant relation)
Centered simple wave / straight characteristics $x=(x'-a)t$ and shock path $x=a\alpha t$
Relation between p and q along the shock locus and its differential
Ratio of differentials of p and q along the shock
Condition on t(p,q) along the shock curve in characteristic coordinates
